text:
Mason Appleton came off injured reserve on Nov. 10, and The Detroit News framed his and Marco Kasper's return as an energy boost for the Red Wings. It hasn't translated yet. Detroit lost both games he played after coming back, and all four games he's played this season have been losses. He has no points and three shots in about ten minutes a night.

Four games is nothing to judge on, but his history explains the role. Appleton is a checker: Evolving-Hockey noted that last season his team created less offense with him on the ice than with almost any other forward (bottom 2%), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said his value, if it's there, shows up away from five-on-five offense. When he does create, it's on the rush (59% of his shots).

The 30-year-old has 465 games of NHL experience before this season, mostly in Winnipeg. On a Detroit team with plenty of turbulence this fall, his job is the unglamorous one: win his matchups, finish checks and leave the scoring to others.
